intro: Biofuels development managers combine engineering, analysis and project leadership, skills used across energy and chemical industries. The closest of the 25 careers below is Chemical Engineers, with an 85% skill match and a BLS May 2025 median of $125,040, and almost every option needs no new degree.
why_it_works: Developing a new fuel or process means testing ideas, judging what will scale and coordinating engineers, suppliers and regulators. O*NET rates complex problem solving, judgment and systems analysis at 3.62 out of 5 for this job. Chemical, energy and industrial engineering use the same analysis. BLS reports this job within a broader group, so this page shows medians instead of percent changes.
tips: Petroleum and Nuclear Engineers earn $144,910 and $133,970, and are 77% matches.
Energy engineering roles are an 81% match and use your fuel and process knowledge.
Practice technology design, such as process modeling software; it is one of your main gaps.

faq.q: What jobs can former biofuels development managers do?
faq.a: The closest matches are Chemical Engineers (85%), water and wastewater engineers (83%) and biofuels production managers (82%), based on O*NET 31.0. Energy engineers are also 81% matched, with a median of $122,930 for their broader BLS group.

faq.q: Which jobs for biofuels managers pay the most?
faq.a: Among the 25 matches, the highest medians are Petroleum Engineers at $144,910, Nuclear Engineers at $133,970 and biofuels production managers at $126,060, according to BLS May 2025 data. Several close matches are reported within broader BLS groups, so compare offers carefully.

faq.q: Do biofuels managers need another degree?
faq.a: Usually not. 23 of the 25 matches need no more education than biofuels development managers already have, including all of the top 10, while 2 need a graduate degree. A bachelor's degree is common, held by 91% of workers in the closest match.

faq.q: What skills should biofuels managers learn?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are operations analysis, complex problem solving, technology design and judgment and decision making. Systems evaluation already rates 3.5 out of 5 for this job in O*NET, so deeper design and process analysis is the main step for engineering roles.
